## Outcome

`cargo check --all-targets` passes with zero errors and zero warnings. `cargo test` passes 151/151 (120 lib + 31 integration), of which **89 are new notification tests**. No test displays a real notification or opens an audio device.

**Structure:** `src-tauri/src/notification/` — `model.rs` (DTOs, sanitization, content policy, audio validation), `permission.rs` (macOS `UNUserNotificationCenter` adapter), `audio.rs` (lazy rodio player), `service.rs` (dispatch/preflight/probe), plus `src-tauri/src/ipc/notifications.rs` with all 7 commands registered in `lib.rs` alongside both plugins.

**Three decisions worth flagging:**

1. **macOS permission is genuinely authoritative.** Section 3.2 of the plan is the crux: `tauri-plugin-notification`'s desktop `permission_state()` hardcodes `Granted`, so it cannot see a user who disabled notifications. I query `UNNotificationSettings` via `objc2-user-notifications` and expose an `authoritative` flag. Only an authoritative `denied` blocks dispatch — a non-authoritative guess never suppresses notifications, which keeps Windows/Linux working.

2. **`currentNotificationCenter()` crashes without a bundle ID.** That call raises an Objective-C exception in any process lacking a bundle identifier — precisely `cargo test` and `cargo run`. I gate on `NSBundle::mainBundle().bundleIdentifier()` and wrap calls in `objc2::exception::catch`, so unbundled runs degrade to non-authoritative instead of aborting. A test asserts the unbundled process never reports authoritative authorization.

3. **Audio dedupe is tested without sleeping.** The 400ms window is exercised by injecting `Instant` values directly rather than timing luck, so the tests are deterministic.

**Two things I corrected against the plan's suggestions:** `NotificationSetting::NotSupported` maps to `None`, not `false` — treating an unsupported sound setting as denied authorization would wrongly block notifications. And zero volume short-circuits before touching the audio device, so muted playback succeeds on machines with no output device (the normal CI case) instead of returning a spurious `no-output-device`.

**One issue you should know about:** while I was working, another concurrent `omo` session was writing to the same files — it overwrote my `mod.rs`, `service.rs`, and `permission.rs` mid-task, and replaced my `rodio` feature list with a bare `rodio = "0.22"` (which pulls in the `recording` feature the plan explicitly says to avoid). Its `permission.rs` also hardcoded macOS to `Authorized`, the exact anti-pattern section 3.2 warns against. I restored my implementation and verified the final state on disk; `cargo tree` confirms `recording`/`rtrb` are excluded. If other agents are still running against this repo, the notification files may get clobbered again — worth serializing those sessions.

Phases 4-9 (TypeScript bridge, settings UI, bell/completion detection, unread state) remain untouched, as scoped.
